title: docs(skills): the UI skill says where a form's column count is authored and where it is derived
body:

_Requested by **Jack** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01EF41AQooqveF2DGD8nqPzS?thread=cmsg_01EF41AQooqveF2DGD8nqPzSUnhXv1JUp4Pnffyiv1ampA)_

Fixes #37629

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：用界面技能搭应用的 AI，被要求「表单每组两列」时不再回答做不到，会在命名表单的分组上写两列，并说明对象自带的新建和编辑弹窗的列数由平台自动决定。
- 为什么做：属于「云端 agent 效果」专题的第一批修复；技能原来说列数一律不能写，三次试验里有两次因此答了做不到。
- 出错会怎样：只改一段说明文字和一条评测用例，写错了 AI 会按错的说法搭表单；撤回这次合并即可恢复原文。
- 要你做什么：不用你批。低风险的技能文字改动，席位在审核通过且检查全绿后落地。

## What changes

`skills/objectstack-ui/rules/navigation.md`, "Record Presentation": the opening paragraph and the "Column count" bullet.

- Before: "Column count. Not authored", for every form.
- After: an object's own New, Edit and detail are built from the object's `fieldGroups`, never from a form view, and their column count is derived. On a named or public form the count is authored per section, `{ group: 'contact_info', columns: 2 }` (1 to 4; one column on a phone). A form view's own `columns` is not read by the form page today.

`skills/objectstack-ui/evals/views-apps-actions-pages.json` gains case 25 (two columns per group on a named form, and what the New dialog does); `evals/README.md` names it. One `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/skills`.

### Premise check: what reads which `columns`

Read on `origin/main` at 33a31dc7, renderer source only, no server booted for this part.

| Surface | Form view's own `columns` | A section's `columns` |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Named form page, `/forms/:name` (`ui/apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx`, `buildSections`) | not read | read (`normalizeColumns(sec.columns)`) |
| Public form, `/f/:slug` (same component) | not read | read |
| An object's New and Edit, dialog and full page | no form view is read at all (`resolveRecordFormChrome` in `ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/recordFormNavigation.ts`); the layout comes from the object's `fieldGroups`, which has no `columns` key | not applicable |
| Setup preview canvas of a form view (`buildFormPreviewSchema` in `.../previews/ViewPreview.tsx`) | read | read |

So the card's premise holds for the skill text and fails for the key it names: `FormViewSchema.columns` parses and is drawn on the preview canvas, and no form a user fills in reads it. The run of the original trial that was counted as "wrote two columns" had written that form-level key. Whether the key is enforced on the form page or retired is not decided here: the seat moved that question to its own decision card, and this pull request leaves `packages/spec/**` and the renderer untouched. The skill sentence about that key says only what is true today.

Three parse probes against the built spec of this branch: a section `{ group: 'basic_info', columns: 2 }` parses; `columns` on a `fieldGroups` entry is refused (`unrecognized_keys`); `columns` on the form view parses.

### Trial case 2, three runs against this branch's skills

Harness from the trial (`harness.mts`, cases 4, 1, 2 in one fresh boot per run, `examples/app-starter`, client `claude -p` on the small model, `mcp__app` and Skill only), skills copied from this branch at 2a30689b; the skills tree at the head below is byte-identical to that commit. Prompt of case 2: split the customer form into "基本信息" and "联系方式", two columns each.

| Run | Answered "cannot be done" | What it saved (published, 0 refusals) | Told the user about the New and Edit dialog |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 1 | no | form view, three sections: `columns: 2`, `columns: 2`, and `columns: 1` for the notes section it kept | no |
| 2 | no | form view, two sections, each `columns: 2` | no |
| 3 | no | form view, two sections, each `columns: 2` | yes: the dialog's count is derived and does not read this form |

Original trial on main: 2 of 3 answered that two columns cannot be done; the third wrote the form-level key. Here 0 of 3 answer that, and 3 of 3 write the section key.

One earlier run on the first commit of this branch (677f9429, whose wording also said an undeclared section draws 2) saved no column count: it grouped through `fieldGroups`, said the New and Edit dialog derives its count, and offered a named form with `{ group, columns: 2 }`. That wording was dropped on the seat's correction, since the undeclared count depends on the pending ruling.

Raw records of all four runs: `trials/haiku-door/rerun-37629/rerun-37629.tgz` in the project files.

Net lines added under `skills/**`: 11 (22 added, 11 removed). The order's budget was 15. The rule file had 10 tokens of headroom; the new words are paid for by shortening the paragraph's rationale ("from the client viewport, because an author, especially an AI, cannot know the client's screen" became "all derived from the client's screen") and by dropping "Author grouping with `fieldGroups`", which the paragraph's closing sentence and the ladder's first step already say.

## Tests

No test pins this passage. The new eval case is a fixture, not an executed test. `git grep` for "Column count" and "column count" under `skills/` finds two other statements, both about the New and Edit dialog and both still true: `rules/list-views.md` ("Dialog size and column count are derived, never authored") and eval case 19.

## Acceptance notes

- Read first: the "Column count" hunk in `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/navigation.md`. The risk is its last sentence, which describes today's renderer and has to be rewritten when the form-level key is ruled on.
- Then the opening paragraph of the same section: "detail" is kept in the list of surfaces built from `fieldGroups`, as before.
- Then eval case 25: `must_contain` pins the section spelling `group: 'contact_info', columns: 2`.
- The heading keeps its text, so the anchor that `rules/list-views.md` links to is unchanged.
- In runs 1 and 2 the assistant did not say that the view it edited (the container's `form` slot, served as `OBJECT.form`) opens nowhere in that app, since no action targets it, and the draft door answered with no advisory. `rules/list-views.md` "Form Views" already states that rule; this pull request does not change it. Noted for the epic's analysis, not filed.
- The card's claim is comment 7198444906 on #37629 (seat epic:#5027#1, branch `claude/project-thread-oddvpd`). It was posted two minutes after this pull request was opened, so the two declaration lines here were copied from the dispatch order, and the first run of the PR-body claim guard read the card before the claim was on it.
- The branch is based on 33a31dc7 and was not merged with `main` again before opening: the eight commits since touch none of these four files.
